title: Python streaming chat: backpressure metrics adapter and operator patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: SDK consumers often integrate streaming chat completions into heterogeneous app architectures (web workers, async queues, microservices) with varying consumption speeds. Without clear backpressure signals and observable metrics, applications either allocate excessive buffering (high memory/cost) or drop/resume incorrectly and create bad UX.

Goal: Design and ship a Python SDK ergonomic primitive (StreamingOperator + BackpressureMetricsAdapter) that: (1) surfaces fine-grained backpressure signals to consumers, (2) emits meaningful telemetry for routing/auto-scaling decisions, (3) integrates with existing resume/checkpoint semantics and idempotent replay tokens, and (4) provides simple examples and migration guidance.

Scope: SDK-facing operator primitives, light-weight metrics adapter (prometheus-friendly counters/gauges/histograms), default SLO-oriented policies (bounded queue, drop-head/slow-path), and example recipes for web-server and background-worker consumption patterns. This ticket covers design, prototype, core API, tests, and one integration example. Follow-ups will add advanced auto-tuning and TypeScript/Go parity.
comments: 2025-02-20 - Ava Chen: Initial write-up. Captured common customer pain: stale UI spinners and OOMs caused by unconstrained streaming buffers. Proposed operator pattern to separate transport events from consumer signals.

2025-02-22 - Ravi Kumar: Implementation plan: add StreamingOperator class in sdk.streaming.operator module; BackpressureMetricsAdapter as an optional hook that registers Prometheus metrics when available. Default operator will expose pause()/resume()/watermark() and an async iterator that yields Event objects (token, delta, done, error).

2025-02-24 - Design review (comments from Maria Lopez): Prefer explicit flow-control semantics over implicit queue size. Suggest APIs: operator.set_consumption_budget(n_tokens) and operator.request_resume_after(bytes_or_ms). Also recommend a lightweight helper that converts operator signals into HTTP chunked backpressure headers for server-side frameworks.

2025-02-26 - Engineering note: Decided to keep the base StreamingOperator sync-friendly: expose both __aiter__ for async consumers and iterate_sync helper for sync code (using thread-safe queue with maximum capacity). This avoids forcing all users into async. Trade-off: slightly more complex tests and thread-safety invariants.

2025-02-27 - Ravi Kumar: Prototype implemented and pushed to branch feat/streaming-operator-backpressure. Added initial tests for bounded queue behavior, pause/resume semantics, and checkpoint token propagation. See GitHub PR in links.

2025-02-28 - QA: Found race when consumer cancels iterator while operator is in paused state. Temporary mitigation: operator.cancel() will wake waiters and mark checkpoint as incomplete. Follow-up to add deterministic shutdown sequence to avoid lost replay tokens.

2025-03-01 - Product (Ivan Petrov): Prioritize example for background-worker ingestion (Celery) and express-style server streaming. Add migration note comparing existing sdk.stream.consume() naive patterns to new operator usage.
2025-03-01 - Ravi Kumar: Marking 'In Progress' — telemetry hooks and PR addressing cancellation race under review.
acceptance_criteria:
1) StreamingOperator provides pause()/resume()/watermark() semantics and interoperates with existing checkpoint/replay token flow.
2) BackpressureMetricsAdapter emits: queue_depth gauge, consumed_tokens counter, stall_duration histogram, and resume_count counter when Prometheus client present.
3) Default operator configuration prevents unbounded memory growth (bounded queue with configurable policy).
4) Unit + integration tests demonstrating: normal flow, slow consumer with pause/resume, cancellation with checkpointing preserved, and example usage in a Flask streaming endpoint and a Celery worker.
5) Docs and migration guide added to SDK docs site.
implementation_notes:
- Module: sdk/streaming/operator.py (StreamingOperator, OperatorEvent)
- Module: sdk/streaming/metrics.py (BackpressureMetricsAdapter)
- Use queue.SimpleQueue + asyncio.Event for cross-thread wakeups; carefully document thread-safety.
- Emit lightweight metrics only when adapter attached to avoid mandatory Prometheus dependency.
- Replay token lifecycle: operator.attach_checkpoint(checkpoint_id:str) will ensure checkpoint included in resume requests and preserved across cancel+resume.
- Provide example utilities: streaming_to_wsgi_chunked() and background_worker_consumer() for quick migration.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus on: (a) API ergonomics for sync vs async consumers, (b) the trade-offs of exposing explicit budget APIs vs implicit high-water marks, and (c) safety of checkpoint propagation during cancel/resume. Link to prototype PR for code-level review.
